title: The archive .gitignore is idempotent by existence not by effect, and the scaffolded .lore/.gitignore still covers cache/ only
description:
Found by an adversarial reviewer during PR #140 (LCLI-467), plus a belt-and-braces suggestion from that PR's implementer. Low severity; grouped because they are the same invariant seen from two ends.

1. writeArchiveGitignore is idempotent by EXISTENCE, not by EFFECT (src/backlog-archive.ts, `if (existsSync(abs)) return;`). An operator who already has a .lore/archive/.gitignore saying anything else -- including one that deliberately un-ignores zips -- silently gets the old false promise back, while the removal prompt still tells them the archive is gitignored. A test currently asserts exactly this skip behaviour, so a future reader will read the hole as intended rather than as a gap. Fix shape: assert the effect (a `git check-ignore -q <zipRel>` after writing) or append rather than skip; and if the behaviour is kept, the test's name should say WHY it is safe to keep.

2. src/core/scaffold.ts's LORE_GITIGNORE still covers `cache/` only (confirmed: it is exactly "cache/\n"). LCLI-467 fixed the ignore AT the archive directory, written when buildArchive runs. Adding `archive/` to the scaffolded .lore/.gitignore would cover repositories before any archive exists. Additive and cheap.

Context for why this matters at all: LCLI-467's prompt copy PROMISES the archive is "gitignored, not committed". Before that PR it was not, in a lore init-scaffolded repo. These two items are what stands between that promise and being conditionally true again.
